text:
mina: Quick proposal — extract the session-tiling logic out of inference-runtime into two smaller services: tiler (hotpath) and metadata-plane (non-hotpath). Goal: reduce hotpath churn, make kv/cache ownership clearer, and speed up runtime deploys.

tj: Why two services instead of a single refactor inside runtime?

mina: Two main reasons: 1) tiler needs ultra-low-latency paths + batching semantics; 2) metadata-plane handles model profiles, routing hints, and slow ops (quant profiles, rollouts) that don't belong in hotpath. Keeping them separate reduces blast radius when changing either.

carmen: Sounds sensible. How do we handle consistency between them for live sessions? Do we need a migration plan for existing session rows?

mina: Plan sketch:
1) Add a façade in runtime that talks to tiler + metadata-plane via short RPCs.
2) Dual-write metadata to both runtime store and metadata-plane for N weeks.
3) Run read-after-write canaries to validate parity.
4) Flip reads to metadata-plane for low-traffic tenants first, ramp up.

mina: Migration note: kv prefix layout needs a small shim — we'll add versioned keys so we can read both v1 (runtime) and v2 (metadata-plane) during migration.

evan: Any perf numbers? Baseline latency impact from adding RPCs to hotpath?

mina: We measured a naive RPC hop adds ~600us p95 on current infra. But tiler will be co-located (same pod or node-local sidecar) to get it down to ~80-150us. Metadata-plane reads are async for most requests; only a tiny set of hot flags are sync.

ops-bot: [deploy-batch] canary-agent detected new image: inference-runtime:tiler-proto-rc1 - started canary deploy to dev cluster.

carmen: What about SLOs and rollbacks? If tiler misbehaves we need immediate fallback to local runtime logic. Can we keep a feature-flag path?

mina: Yes — feature flag + runtime fallback. Runtime will have a small cached fallback implementation of tiling for emergency switch. We'll add a quick toggle with immediate effect and also an automatic failover if RPC latencies spike.

sara: Owners? timeline? and any changes to pricing/infra cost?

mina: Owners: tj -> tiler runtime integration + latency work; carmen -> metadata-plane API + migration; evan -> rollout automation + canaries. Timeline: prototype spike in 2 weeks, canary in staging week 5, limited prod ramp week 7–8. Infra cost: small increase from one extra pod per node pool during ramp, then should be neutral or slightly cheaper due to better caching.

carmen: For migration dual-write, we should add a regression test that asserts eventual consistency within 5s for a sample workload. Also add a consumer that replays mismatches.

mina: Agreed. I'll add tests to the migration checklist. Example migration toggles:

```
# enable dual-write for tenant X
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -X POST "https://admin.internal/feature-flags" -d '{"flag":"tiler_dual_write","tenant":"tenant-x","state":"on"}'

# flip reads
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/feature-flags" -d '{"flag":"tiler_reads","tenant":"tenant-x","state":"on"}'
```

carmen: Nice. On the schema side, metadata-plane will own model_profile and quant_profile objects? We should define a small compatibility contract (read-only fields, canonical owner).

mina: Exactly — metadata-plane will be canonical for model_profile, quant_profile, rollout_state. Runtime will keep a short-lived cache and the fallback keyspace. Contract doc will live in RFC repo and link from the PR.

evan: I can start the canary automation and add latency-based abort rules (p95>2x baseline or error-rate>0.5%).

tj: I'll prototype co-located tiler as a sidecar first to prove latency. If that looks good we can discuss moving to same-pod container vs separate process.

ops-bot: [canary] deployment inference-runtime:tiler-proto-rc1 - 3/3 canary pods up, p95 latency: +120us vs baseline.

mina: Good initial numbers. Next actions: create RFC doc w/ contracts, submit two spike PRs (tiler sidecar proto, metadata-plane api stub), and produce a migration checklist with tests.

sara: ok please add me to the RFC review and calendar the spike demo.

mina: Will do. Anyone else want to volunteer for the migration replay consumer?

evan: I'll pick that up after canary setup.

carmen: I'll start drafting the API contract.

tj: I'll schedule a latency spike test next week.

mina: Thanks all. Keeping the rollout incremental and feature-flag driven should keep risk low. :thumbsup: :shipit:
